name: Neo-Assyrian Empire (Esarhaddon)

territory.border: hb:bc700:Assyria + hb:bc700:Babylonia + hb:bc700:Arameans + hb:bc700:Kingdom of David and Solomon

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 1,400,000 km2 for 911-612 BCE; Taagepera 1978 and Turchin 2006 give 1.4 million km2 at 670 BCE (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_empires). The historical-basemaps world_bc700 file has only a core 'Assyria' polygon (174,000 km2), so the border unions Assyria + Babylonia + Arameans + Kingdom of David and Solomon (Levant) = ~877,000 km2 computed from the GeoJSON (low side); western Iran, Cilicia and Lower Egypt (conquered 671) are missing from the polygon and Susa (Elamite) is wrongly included.

population.note: Seshat codes 5,000,000-7,000,000 for 670 BCE (mid = midpoint). High allows Lower Egypt, held 671-669.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Seshat codes the largest settlement (Nineveh) at 120,000 for 700 BCE; Assyrian capitals were very large, the periphery rural.

activePersonnel.note: Dalley 2017 (p. 531, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire): the number of soldiers was likely several hundred thousand at the empire's height; Healy 1991 (p. 23, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_Neo-Assyrian_Empire): capable of 120,000+ (Shalmaneser III's boast of 120,000 men). Composition anchor: Qarqar 853 BCE, Gabriel 2002-2003 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Qarqar) gives the Assyrian side 35,000 incl. 20,000 infantry, 12,000 cavalry (sic) and 1,200 chariots. Army = central standing army (kisir sarri) plus provincial contingents raised by governors and vassal troops (Dalley 2017 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire). Mid = standing army, garrisons and provincial contingents in service in 670 (Egyptian and Median frontiers active); high toward Dalley's 'several hundred thousand'.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Provincial levies callable within a month.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Chariot crews (3-4 per vehicle), engineers and sappers, interpreters, guides, supply train, scribes.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Provincial levies (ilku service), deportee soldiers and vassal contingents; a heavily militarised tributary empire.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Dalley 2017 (p. 531, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire): the number of soldiers was likely several hundred thousand at the empire's height; Healy 1991 (p. 23, cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_Neo-Assyrian_Empire): capable of 120,000+ (Shalmaneser III's boast of 120,000 men). Composition anchor: Qarqar 853 BCE, Gabriel 2002-2003 (via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Qarqar) gives the Assyrian side 35,000 incl. 20,000 infantry, 12,000 cavalry (sic) and 1,200 chariots. Army = central standing army (kisir sarri) plus provincial contingents raised by governors and vassal troops (Dalley 2017 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire). Split: heavy and medium spearmen in close formation ~33% of the personnel roles (Dalley 2017 pp. 526-528 for the infantry types).

quality.note: Iron weapons, pointed iron helmets, scale armour for heavy infantry: the era's best (rubric 0.75-1.0).

training.note: Standing royal regiments professional (0.75), provincial contingents less.

quality.note: Lance, sword, scale armour; horse armour under Ashurbanipal.

Chariot numbers: 1,200 at Qarqar in 853 (Gabriel); by 670 chariots were fewer relative to cavalry and used as heavy shock and command vehicles. Crews in supportPersonnel.
Educated guess. Siege engines: wheeled battering rams with archer turrets and siege towers, a signature Assyrian arm in the reliefs; no count survives.

quality.note: Best siege engines of the era before torsion artillery.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: trained staff (turtanu, rab shaqe), intelligence networks, campaign planning; Esarhaddon took Memphis in 671.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: professional core with strong identity, large share of deportee and vassal troops.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: imperial confidence, recent conquest of Egypt.

weapons.note: Near anchor 3: iron weapons in general use, siege engines; no torsion artillery.

armor.note: Between 2 and 3: iron scale armour, iron helmets, horse armour.

ships.note: Between 2 and 3: relied on Phoenician vassal galleys.

fortification.note: Near anchor 3: massive walled capitals (Nineveh 12 km circuit), siege towers.

logistics.note: Near anchor 3: royal roads with stations, depot provisioning before campaigns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire).

communications.note: Anchor 3: state relay-post system and fire signals (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Assyrian_Empire).

isr.note: Between 2 and 3: interpreters, guides, spy reports from governors.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 via https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true: Iraq, Iran, Israel 1 CE = 1,116 (2011 int$); Iraq 730 CE = 1,466. Applied ~670 years earlier.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Highly militarised tributary empire; tribute and booty financed much of it.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Large palace workshops, iron working, monumental building.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Rain-fed northern plains plus irrigated Babylonia; drought stress in the heartland late in the period.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; Bronze Age life expectancy was if anything lower, so this is not an underestimate.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Royal roads (harran sharri) with stations linking the provinces; engineered stretches, total length undocumented.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Phoenician and Philistine vassal ports (Sidon/Kar-Esarhaddon, Arwad, Byblos, Gaza).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Phoenician merchant shipping under Assyrian control.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Pre-stocked campaign depots and vassal provisioning; Esarhaddon's march to Egypt crossed the Sinai with Arab camel supply.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses (imported in thousands), mules, donkeys, camels, oxen; ~0.08-0.2 per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: fortified capitals, local supply; subject provinces disloyal.

notes: Snapshot = 670 BCE, Esarhaddon after the conquest of Memphis (671); Taharqa retook it in 669. Forces = standing army plus provincial contingents in service. Royal inscriptions (Shalmaneser's 120,000; deportation totals) are not used as mids; scholarly totals are qualitative ('several hundred thousand'), so counts are grade C reconstructions. Population convention: everything inside the empire per Seshat; the border union understates the empire's real extent.
